【参考范文 · 160 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Nowadays, cultivating independent learning ability is becoming increasingly crucial for personal development. As knowledge updates at an unprecedented pace, the skills we master at school can no longer carry us through an entire career, which makes the capacity to learn on our own a decisive advantage.
To begin with, self-directed learning keeps us competitive. Those who can teach themselves new tools quickly adapt to changing workplaces, while those who wait to be taught inevitably fall behind. Take my own experience: when our university suddenly shifted to online courses, I taught myself data analysis through free tutorials, and that skill later helped me stand out in an internship. Moreover, lifelong learning nurtures independent thinking, enabling us to judge information critically rather than swallow it blindly.
In conclusion, independent learning is far more than an academic skill; it is a lifelong engine that drives personal growth. Therefore, we should consciously develop this ability and treat every day as a chance to learn.

lines.en: W: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
lines.zh: W: 谢谢你在这么短的时间内抽空见我，Stephen。

lines.en: M: Not a problem, Margaret. Now, please give me some good news. Have you agreed to my last proposal?
lines.zh: M: 没问题，Margaret。现在，请告诉我一些好消息。你同意我上次的提议了吗？

lines.en: W: I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
lines.zh: W: 确实同意了。我希望签署协议，前提是对合同做一处小改动。

lines.en: M: Margaret, we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations. Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients, or not? I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
lines.zh: M: Margaret，我们为这件事来回磋商、不断修改，已经快一年了。你到底确定要为你的客户达成一项赞助协议，还是不想？我之所以这样问，是因为坦率地说，我这边有些人已经快失去耐心了。

lines.en: W: I understand your concerns. But as I'm sure you understand, we hold our clients' best interests to be of the utmost concern. We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
lines.zh: W: 我理解你的担忧。不过，我相信你也明白，我们最关心的是客户的最大利益。因此，我们会仔细审阅所有合同的细节，请放心，我们都很感谢贵公司的耐心。

lines.en: M: OK, fine. So what change do you wish to make?
lines.zh: M: 好吧，没问题。那么你想做什么改动？

lines.en: W: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East. That's all.
lines.zh: W: 基本上，我们希望新协议不包括中东地区。就这些。

lines.en: M: The Middle East? Why?
lines.zh: M: 中东地区？为什么？

lines.en: W: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East. Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only. Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
lines.zh: W: 我的客户还收到几家中东公司的其他潜在营销合作邀约。如果这些邀约最终落实，对方将只在中东地区使用我客户的形象。因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保这两项营销活动在地域上不会重叠。

lines.en: M: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
lines.zh: M: 你说的中东业务具体属于哪个行业？

lines.en: W: Real estate.
lines.zh: W: 房地产。

lines.en: M: Well, that should be okay then. So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest. Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people. I don't foresee any problem, though. The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
lines.zh: M: 那应该没问题。只要产品与我们的食品和饮料市场有很大不同，就不应存在利益冲突。不过，我还是得把这件事拿去和我的团队确认一下。但我预计不会有什么问题。中东对我们来说是个微不足道的市场，不过我仍然需要和几个部门核实一下。

lines.en: M: Next, we have a special science-related news story. Paula Hancocks at the Denver Observatory. Paula, what is the big story over there?
lines.zh: M：接下来是一则特别的科学新闻报道。丹佛天文台的 Paula Hancocks，Paula，那边有什么重大新闻？

lines.en: W: Hi, John. Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited. In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky.
lines.zh: W：你好，John。是的，这里的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。事实上，整个北美以及北半球其他地区的太空爱好者今晚都会聚集到山顶，观看夜空。

lines.en: M: Why? What's the big event? Is there an eclipse happening soon?
lines.zh: M：为什么？有什么重大事件？很快要发生日食了吗？

lines.en: W: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years. For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
lines.zh: W：今晚，地球将与 Oppenheimer 彗星近距离接近。这是100多年来我们的星球距离此类现象最近的一次。因此，预计今晚会有数千人仰望天空，观看这个令人震撼的天体。

lines.en: M: How far away is this comet? Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
lines.zh: M：这颗彗星距离我们有多远？人们用肉眼能看到它吗？

lines.en: W: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy. But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope. People will only see a blur without one. However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment. Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
lines.zh: W：Oppenheimer 彗星仍会位于数百万英里之外，在我们银河系的边缘。不过，这仍然算是相对较近的距离，近到人们可以通过望远镜清楚地观测它。没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到一团模糊的影像。不过，这并不意味着必须使用专业设备。即使是最普通的望远镜，也足以让人们观测并惊叹于这个飞行中的天体。

lines.en: M: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event. Where will this comet be in the sky? How can people find it?
lines.zh: M：我们的许多观众都会想知道，他们怎样才能参与这场一生难遇的活动。这颗彗星会出现在天空的什么位置？人们该如何找到它？

lines.en: W: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator. However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky. And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
lines.zh: W：这颗彗星几乎正好位于正北方，在赤道上方60度的位置。不过，找到这颗彗星确实非常困难。这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用可以帮助大家定位。

lines.en: M: How fantastic! Thank you, Paula, for the information.
lines.zh: M：太棒了！Paula，感谢你提供这些信息。

lines.en: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world. While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
lines.zh: 膳食指南构成了世界各地营养建议和相关法规的基础。尽管现有大多数指南背后都有强有力的科学共识，但最近有一个问题引发了争议：是否应当提醒消费者避免食用超加工食品？

lines.en: Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems. The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14th during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE.
lines.zh: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文，分别阐述了支持和反对使用“超加工食品”这一概念的理由，以帮助在传统食品分类体系之外进一步制定膳食指南。论文作者、圣保罗大学的Carlos Monteiro和Novo Nordisk Foundation的Arne Astrup，将于8月14日在NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE期间举行的线上直播辩论中讨论这一问题。

lines.en: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed. The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product. Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
lines.zh: 这场辩论围绕Monteiro及其同事制定的一套体系展开，该体系根据食品的工业加工程度对其进行分类，范围从未加工食品到超加工食品。该体系将超加工食品定义为：通过一系列加工步骤制成的食品，在这些步骤中，先从食品中提取物质，再使用化学品对其进行改变，以配制出最终产品。超加工食品通常被设计成价格低廉、美味可口且方便食用；其中包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、即热食品以及再制肉制品等。

lines.en: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are packed high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet. While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
lines.zh: 研究表明，食用超加工食品会导致体重增加并提高患慢性疾病的风险；这类食品含有大量盐、糖和脂肪，即使在对膳食中盐、糖和脂肪的含量进行调整后，这些关联仍然存在。尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未被完全理解，Monteiro认为，现有证据已经足以支持在膳食建议和政府政策中劝阻人们食用超加工食品。

lines.en: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints. According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently. With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully. When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
lines.zh: 信不信由你，限制有益于人类的创造力。心理学家认为，当你可利用的资源较少时，你实际上会开始以不同的方式看待世界。有了限制，你会将 mental energy 投入到更具资源性地采取行动上。面对挑战时，你会想出新的方法，让自己做得更好。

lines.en: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher. People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do. They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further. Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use. They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
lines.zh: 最成功的创意人士知道，限制会促使他们的思维跃得更高。发明新产品的人不会受到自己没有什么或不能做什么的限制。他们利用自身的局限，推动自己更进一步。许多产品和服务之所以诞生，是因为创始人发现自己所使用的产品或服务存在局限。他们根据当时对自己不起作用的地方创造了创新。

lines.en: Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation. In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways. When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to. Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes. Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
lines.zh: 创新是创意人士对局限的回应。在一项于2015年开展的研究中，伊利诺伊大学的Ravi Mehta和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的Meng Zhu考察了对稀缺或富足的思考如何影响人们创造性地使用资源，并发现人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式利用手头的资源。当人们面临资源稀缺时，他们会迫使自己以不那么传统的方式使用资源，因为他们不得不这样做。障碍可以拓宽你的认知，并开启你的思维过程。持续存在的限制有助于你提高将不相关的想法和概念联系起来的能力。

lines.en: Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, "Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained."
lines.zh: 谷歌前搜索产品和用户体验副总裁Marissa Mayer曾在彭博社的一篇刊物中写道：“限制能够塑造问题、聚焦问题，并提供有待克服的明确挑战；创造力在受到限制时最能蓬勃发展。”

lines.en: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts. These strategies are learned in childhood. Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations. We just do whatever seems to come naturally. But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person. How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict. Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
lines.zh: 不同的人会采用不同的冲突处理策略。这些策略是在童年时期学会的。通常，我们并没有意识到自己在冲突情境中是如何行动的，只是按照看似自然而然的方式去做。但我们确实都有自己的策略，而且由于这种策略是后天习得的，所以我们始终可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。当你卷入冲突时，有两个主要方面需要考虑：实现个人目标，以及与对方保持良好关系。个人目标对你的重要程度，以及这段关系对你的重要程度，都会影响你在冲突中的行为。根据这两个方面，可以确定五种冲突处理风格。

lines.en: The turtle. Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts. They give up their personal goals and relationships. They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
lines.zh: 龟型。乌龟会缩进壳里以避免冲突。它们放弃个人目标和人际关系。它们认为，与其面对冲突，不如退出冲突更容易。

lines.en: The shark. Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict. They seek to achieve their goals at all costs. Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing. Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement. Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
lines.zh: 鲨鱼型。鲨鱼试图迫使对方接受自己提出的冲突解决方案，从而压倒对方。它们不惜一切代价追求实现自己的目标。鲨鱼认为，冲突的解决方式是一方获胜、另一方失败。获胜会让鲨鱼产生自豪感和成就感；失败则会让它们感到软弱、无能和挫败。

lines.en: The teddy bear. Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people. They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships. They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
lines.zh: 泰迪熊型。泰迪熊希望得到他人的接纳和喜爱。它们认为，为了保持和谐，应当避免冲突，并相信讨论冲突会损害人际关系。它们放弃自己的目标，以维护这段关系。

lines.en: The fox. Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people. They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals. They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
lines.zh: 狐狸型。狐狸对自身目标以及与他人的关系都抱有适度的关注。它们放弃一部分自己的目标，并说服冲突中的对方也放弃一部分目标。它们寻求一种能让双方都获得一些利益的冲突解决方案。

lines.en: The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved. They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people. They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem. By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship. Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
lines.zh: 猫头鹰型。猫头鹰把冲突视为需要解决的问题。它们认为，冲突能够通过减少两个人之间的紧张关系来改善人际关系。它们试图展开讨论，将冲突界定为一个问题。通过寻求既能满足自己又能满足对方的解决方案，猫头鹰得以维持这段关系。在找到既能实现自己的目标、又能实现对方目标的解决方案之前，猫头鹰不会感到满意；在紧张情绪和负面感受得到彻底解决之前，它们也不会感到满意。

lines.en: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health. Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops in agriculture, and create new bio-materials.
lines.zh: 地球上现存的全部150万种已知动植物的遗传密码将被测序，以帮助拯救濒临灭绝的物种并促进人类健康。科学家希望，破解动植物的遗传密码能够帮助发现传染病的新疗法、延缓衰老、改良农业作物，并创造新的生物材料。

lines.en: In Britain, organizations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants. Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million. Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
lines.zh: 在英国，包括自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和Wellcome Sanger研究所在内的多个组织已经联合起来，为英国的6.6万种动植物进行基因测序。该项目被称为“达尔文生命之树项目”，预计将耗时10年，耗资1亿英镑。项目完成后，所有信息都将向研究人员公开。

lines.en: Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500. It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago. Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionise the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
lines.zh: 许多科学家认为，地球如今已经进入第六次大灭绝时期，人类造成的栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的有害结合，已经导致自1500年以来至少77种哺乳动物和140种鸟类灭绝。这是自6600万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大规模的物种损失。科学家表示，对每一个物种进行测序将彻底改变人们对生物学和进化的认识，加强保护以及维护和恢复生物多样性的努力。

lines.en: Dr. Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said, "Whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup. How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it. We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past. And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future."
lines.zh: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部负责人蒂姆·利特尔伍德博士说：“无论你对食物还是疾病感兴趣，地球上每一种生物如何适应其环境的历史，都记录在它的遗传构成中。你如何利用这些信息，取决于你理解它的能力。我们将运用现代方法，真正清晰地了解现在和过去。当然，了解过去也能为未来提供一个预测模型。”

lines.en: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project. Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60 percent of animal populations. About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction. We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply. As scientists, we all realise we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now. I think we're making history."
lines.zh: Wellcome科学部主任吉姆·史密斯爵士说：“尽管我努力思考，也想不出还有哪个项目比这更加令人兴奋、更加贴近现实、更加及时，或更能激发国际社会的灵感。自1970年以来，人类已经使动物种群数量减少了60%。在接受调查的8万种物种中，约有2.3万种正走向灭绝。我们正处于地球生命第六次大灭绝事件之中，这不仅威胁野生动物物种，也危及全球粮食供应。作为科学家，我们都意识到，现在迫切需要为我们这个脆弱星球上的生命编制目录。我认为，我们正在创造历史。”

lines.en: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main." Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self", and not even our bodies are truly "us".
lines.zh: 英国诗人约翰·多恩在17世纪写道：“没有人是一座孤岛，自成一体；每个人都是大陆的一部分，是陆地的一部分。”如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体性确实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、身体和文化层面的相互联系，远比人们意识到的更加紧密。在他的新书《The Self Delusion》中，雷丁大学生态学与进化研究组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授认为，根本不存在所谓的“自我”，甚至连我们的身体也并不真正是“我们”。

lines.en: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity. "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution," he writes. "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have an unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you. This is the illusion I seek to tackle. We are intimately connected to the world around us."
lines.zh: 正如哥白尼意识到地球并不是宇宙的中心一样，奥利弗教授说，社会迫切需要一场类似哥白尼革命的变革，以理解人并非彼此孤立的存在，而是同一个相互联系的身份的一部分。他写道：“人类心智文化演化中的一个重要里程碑，是人们接受地球并不是宇宙的中心，这就是所谓的哥白尼革命。然而，我们还需要摒弃另一个重大的神话：我们以独立自我的身份存在于主观宇宙的中心。你可能会觉得自己是一个独立的个体，在世界上自主行动；觉得自己拥有一个终生持续不变的内在自我，作为一个中心锚点，而世界则在你周围不断变化。这正是我试图应对的幻觉。我们与周围的世界有着密切的联系。”

lines.en: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years. "Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity."
lines.zh: 奥利弗教授认为，人体内大约有37万亿个细胞，但其中大多数的寿命只有几天或几周，因此构成“我们”的物质一直在变化。事实上，你身体的任何部分都没有存在超过10年。“由于我们的身体本质上每隔几周就会重新形成，仅凭其中的物质显然不足以解释身份持续存在的脉络。”

lines.en: Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems. Through selfish over-consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate. "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behaviour to act in less selfish ways," he said. "So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us."
lines.zh: 奥利弗教授声称，个人主义实际上不利于社会，只有意识到我们是更大实体的一部分，才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。我们通过自私的过度消费正在摧毁自然世界，并以越来越快的速度消耗不可再生资源。他说：“作为一个物种，我们正处于关键的十字路口，必须迅速改变我们的思维方式和行为，以更加不自私的方式行事。因此，让我们睁开双眼，看清周围隐藏的各种联系。”

analysis.定位: P1 But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts. 但我们确实有一套个人策略，而正因为它是后天习得的，我们总能通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?

analysis.定位: P1 The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health. 地球上全部 150 万已知动植物物种的基因密码都将被绘制出来，以帮助拯救物种免于灭绝、并提升人类健康。
analysis.信号: 目的信号 to help 后面接落点。答案句靠目的状语 to help save species from extinction and boost human health 中的 to help 锁定——"做基因测序"的目的正写在 to help 之后，这正是题干 hope to do 要的那一层。
analysis.替换: save species from extinction and boost human health↔Help save species from extinction and boost human health.选项几乎原句搬来，只在前面加 Help

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do many scientists believe with regard to earth?
questions.stem_zh: 许多科学家对地球持什么看法?

analysis.定位: P3 Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change. 许多科学家相信，地球如今已进入第六次大规模物种灭绝，人类制造出栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化交织而成的有毒组合。
analysis.信号: 观点信号 Many scientists believe 直接引出。答案句由 Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction 这个观点引导句锁定——题干 believe 与原文 believe 对齐，believe 后的 that 从句就是"许多科学家相信什么"的答案。
analysis.替换: earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction↔It has entered the sixth mass extinction.earth→It，其余原句保留
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱It was once dominated by dinosaurs. 蹭录音里的 dinosaurs，但原文说的是 the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago——恐龙是被灭绝来做"损失之大"的参照，录音从没说"地球曾被恐龙统治"，纯属听到 dinosaurs 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago C)偷换概念Its prospects depend on future human behaviour. 说"地球前景取决于未来人类行为"，录音第 4 段虽提到 a window on the future，但那是讲项目能模型化未来，并非"许多科学家相信地球前景取决于人类未来行为"，把别处的零碎拼成新断言，无中生有。 借用原文：a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future D)原词陷阱Its climate change is aggravated by humans. 抓住录音 habitat loss, pollution and climate change 里的 climate change 单独放大，但原文是"栖息地丧失、污染、气候变化"三者并列、共同构成有毒组合，单拎一项当作"科学家相信地球如何"，以偏概全。 借用原文：a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change

questions.stem: 【题目】 How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?
questions.stem_zh: Wellcome科学主任Jim Smith爵士如何描述生命之树计划?

analysis.定位: P5 Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project." Wellcome 科学总监 Jim Smith 爵士说："无论我怎么想，都想不出还有比这更激动人心、更切题、更及时、更具国际启发性的项目。"
analysis.信号: 评价语气：I can't think of a more… 是变相最高级。答案句靠 I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project 这个"想不出更…的"否定结构锁定——"想不出比它更…的"等于"它是最…的"，是说话人对项目的最高评价。
analysis.替换: I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project↔It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational."想不出更…的"="最…的"，比较级转最高级
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth. 蹭了录音 conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity 的原词，但说"它使其它一切保护努力相形见绌"是录音没有的比较，且这是 Jim Smith 的评价题，A 拼的是别处第 3 段的料，张冠李戴。 借用原文：bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity B)答非所问It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists. 蹭了录音 cost £100 million 与众多科学家协作的料，但这是讲项目的成本与规模，是客观事实，不是 Jim Smith"如何形容/评价"项目，答非所问。 借用原文：it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million C)过度推断It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct. 用了录音常出现的"动植物灭绝"原词，但录音只说项目能助保护、记录生命，从没说能"把已灭绝物种带回来"，明显过度推断。 借用原文：we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now

questions.stem: 【题目】 What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver?
questions.stem_zh: 根据Tom Oliver教授的观点,什么实际上只是一种幻觉?

analysis.定位: P1 Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise. 如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体独立性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面上的相互联系远比人们意识到的紧密。
analysis.信号: 原句直陈定性。答案句直接用 human individuality is indeed just an illusion 把某概念点定为"幻觉"，is just an illusion 这种判定句就是信号，听到"X 其实只是个幻觉"就锁定 X。
analysis.替换: human individuality↔Human individuality.原词直接对应
analysis.排除: C)原词陷阱The Copernican revolution. 盗用了录音第二段反复出现的 Copernican，但哥白尼革命是讲者用来作类比的"参照"，不是被称为幻觉的对象，属听到 Copernican 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：the so-called Copernican Revolution B)原词陷阱Social evolution. 借了录音 the cultural evolution of human minds 里的 evolution 一词，但"社会／文化演化"是讲者描述心智发展的背景，并未被定性为幻觉。 借用原文：A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds A)偷换概念Cultural identity. 与录音 cultural level 的 cultural 沾边，但讲者说的是"文化层面的联系"，从未把"文化身份"称为幻觉，属偷换概念。 借用原文：at a mental, physical, and cultural level

locate.en: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise.
locate.zh: 如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体独立性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面上的相互联系远比人们意识到的紧密。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe?
questions.stem_zh: Tom Oliver教授如何看待我们作为独立自我存在于主观宇宙中心这一观念?

analysis.定位: P2 However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe. 然而，我们还有一个大迷思需要破除：即我们以为自己是独立的自我、处在一个主观宇宙的中心。
analysis.信号: 转折However后是真意。句首 However 转折之后才是讲者真正要表达的态度，他把那个想法称为 one more big myth to dispose of（又一个要破除的迷思），处置动词 dispose of 直接给出否定态度。
analysis.替换: one more big myth to dispose of↔a delusion to be disposed ofmyth=delusion同义替换
analysis.排除: D)原词陷阱rooted in the mindset of the 17th century 盗用了录音开头 wrote in the 17th century 的时间词，但 17 世纪说的是 John Donne 写诗的年代，讲者从未说那个"独立自我"的想法植根于 17 世纪心态，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：wrote in the 17th century C)张冠李戴a myth spread by John Donne's poem 把"迷思"归因到 John Donne 的诗，盗用了开头出现的 John Donne，但讲者引 Donne 的诗恰恰是支持"人互相连接"，并非说这首诗散布了迷思，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main B)未提及prevalent even among academics（连学者中都很普遍）原文从未提及，讲者只说这是普遍的 illusion，没有专门强调"在学者中尤其普遍"，属未提及。

locate.en: However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe.
locate.zh: 然而，我们还有一个大迷思需要破除：即我们以为自己是独立的自我、处在一个主观宇宙的中心。

a myth spread by John Donne's poem 把"迷思"归因到 John Donne 的诗，盗用了开头出现的 John Donne，但讲者引 Donne 的诗恰恰是支持"人互相连接"，并非说这首诗散布了迷思，属张冠李戴。
rooted in the mindset of the 17th century 盗用了录音开头 wrote in the 17th century 的时间词，但 17 世纪说的是 John Donne 写诗的年代，讲者从未说那个"独立自我"的想法植根于 17 世纪心态，属原词陷阱。

questions.stem: 【题目】 Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material "us" is constantly changing?

analysis.定位: P3 Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing. 奥利弗教授指出，人体内约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物质意义上的"我们"在不断变化。
analysis.信号: 因果so前是原因。句中 so the material "us" is constantly changing 的 so 是结果标志，so 之前的 most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks 就是讲者给出的原因，正是 Why 题要找的依据句。
analysis.替换: most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks↔most of our body cells can only live a few days or weekslifespan改写为can only live
analysis.排除: B)原词陷阱ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading 盗用了录音第一段介绍学者时的 the University of Reading，但那只是说明他的任职单位，原文从未说他在该校获得了大量科学证据，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading A)答非所问He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe. 又借 Copernican 一词，但本题问的是"物质之我为何在变"，答案是细胞寿命，与哥白尼无关，属答非所问。 借用原文：Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe C)偷换概念He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected. 听上去与全篇"互相连接"主旨呼应，但原文并未以"内在自我与物质自我相连"来解释物质之我为何变化，是偷换概念、答非所问。 借用原文：We are intimately connected to the world around us.

questions.stem: 【题目】 How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?
questions.stem_zh: 根据Tom Oliver教授的观点,我们如何才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题?

analysis.定位: P4 Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems. 奥利弗教授声称，个人主义其实对社会有害，只有意识到我们是更大整体的一部分，我们才能解决紧迫的环境与社会问题。

cloze.title: 2024年6月·第1套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: It's quite remarkable how different genres of music can spark unique feelings, emotions, and memories. Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries and we are all attracted toward our own unique life soundtrack.
passages.zh: 不同音乐流派能够唤起独特的感受、情绪和记忆，这一点相当令人惊叹。研究表明，音乐可以减轻手术前的压力和焦虑，而我们都会被属于自己的独特人生配乐所吸引。

passages.en: If you're looking to __(26)__ stress, you might want to give classical music a try.
passages.zh: 如果你想缓解压力，不妨试试听听古典音乐。

passages.en: The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain that helps control attention, learning and emotional responses. It can also turn down the body's stress response, resulting in an overall happier mood. It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to __(28)__ in a person's thinking.
passages.zh: 古典音乐的声音会产生镇静作用，使大脑释放引发愉悦的多巴胺，从而帮助控制注意力、学习和情绪反应。它还可以降低身体的应激反应，使人的整体情绪更加愉快。事实证明，愉悦的情绪能够使人的思维更加清晰。

passages.en: Although there are many great __(29)__ of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel, none of these artists' music seems to have the same health effects as Mozart's does. According to researchers, listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve __(30)__ function. Another study found that the distinctive features of Mozart's music trigger parts of the brain that are responsible for high-level mental functions. Even maternity __(31)__ use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother's belly.
passages.zh: 尽管古典音乐有许多伟大的作曲家，如巴赫、贝多芬和亨德尔，但这些艺术家的音乐似乎都没有莫扎特的音乐那样具有相同的健康功效。据研究人员称，聆听莫扎特的音乐可以增强脑电波活动并改善认知功能。另一项研究发现，莫扎特音乐的独特特征能够激活负责高级心理功能的大脑区域。甚至产科病房也会使用莫扎特的音乐，帮助新生儿适应母亲子宫外的生活。

passages.en: It has been found that listening to classical music __(32)__ reduces a person's blood pressure. Researchers believe that the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart __(33)__ from stress. Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping. One study found that students who had trouble sleeping slept better while they were listening to classical music.
passages.zh: 研究发现，聆听古典音乐能够显著降低人的血压。研究人员认为，古典音乐的舒缓声音可能有助于心脏从压力中恢复。古典音乐还可以成为帮助睡眠困难者的一个很好的工具。一项研究发现，睡眠有困难的学生在听古典音乐时睡得更好。

passages.en: Whether classical music is something that you listen to on a regular basis or not, it wouldn't __(34)__ to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__ . You will be surprised at how good it makes you feel and the potentially positive change in your health.
passages.zh: 无论你是否经常听古典音乐，抽出一些时间来听让自己感到舒缓的音乐都不会有坏处。它给你带来的良好感受以及对健康可能产生的积极改变，会让你感到惊讶。

wordbank.gloss: 减轻、缓解（不适、痛苦、压力等）
（动）伤害、有害；在 it wouldn't hurt to do 句式中表「做……无妨/不会有坏处」
舒缓的、令人安心的；抚慰（人）
（名）（医院的）病房、病区；（动，三单）守护

rows.text: A) alleviate动词
be looking to + 动词原形 + stress

alleviate stress=缓解压力，是固定搭配 If you're looking to __(26)__ stress, you might want to give classical music a try. 与开篇 Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries 中的 reduce stress 同义改写，alleviate stress 在英语里就是「减轻压力」的标准说法。
L)recover搭配错位：通常 recover from stress，不直接 recover stress recover 表「从……恢复」时几乎都用 recover from sth，直接接 stress 不合英语习惯；且本句要表达的是「减轻」而非「恢复」压力。
I) loose动词
letting + 空 + 名词短语（pleasure-inducing dopamine）
loose dopamine=释放多巴胺 letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain，loose 这里作动词意为「释放」，与「大脑释放令人愉悦的多巴胺」语义完美对应，也呼应 produce a calming effect 的因果链。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— 看到 letting 容易误以为后跟 -ing 并列。考生可能把 letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain 误读成两个 -ing 并列，从而填 inhibiting；但 let + 宾语 + 动词原形才是正解，且 inhibiting 与「释放多巴胺」语义相反，是典型反向干扰。
B) clarity名词
lead to + 空 + in a person's thinking
clarity in thinking=思维清晰 It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to __(28)__ in a person's thinking. 中 clarity in (one's) thinking 是英语固定表达，意思是「思路清晰」，与「愉悦情绪带来思维清晰」的因果链贴合，也承接前文古典音乐的认知促进作用。
D) composers名词
many great + 空 + of classical music + 人名举例
三位人名=三位作曲家的上义词 like Bach, Beethoven and Handel 是教科书级的古典作曲家清单，composers 与之构成「上义词—举例」的关系，语义和复数形态都完美对上。
C) cognitive形容词
improve + 空 + function（名词）

cognitive function=认知功能，脑科学固定搭配 listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve __(30)__ function. 与前文 brain wave activity、以及后文 high-level mental functions 同主题串联，cognitive function 是脑科学英语中最常见的搭配，意为「认知功能」。
J)majestic义为「雄伟壮丽」，与脑功能不搭 majestic 用来修饰山川宫殿等宏伟事物，与 function 搭配语义不通，且本段讨论的是大脑健康，不存在审美维度。 K)mandatory义为「强制的」，与「improve」宾语逻辑冲突 mandatory function 意思变成「强制功能」，与「听莫扎特改善大脑功能」的因果链完全错位。
O) wards名词
maternity + 空 + use…
maternity wards 固定搭配=产科病房 Even maternity __(31)__ use Mozart to help newborn babies 中「产科病房放莫扎特给新生儿听」是常识场景，wards 与 maternity 形成医院科室专名，语义、形态、搭配三对齐。
M) significantly副词
主谓之间修饰谓语动词的位置
实验结论描述效果 → 显著地 It has been found that listening to classical music __(32)__ reduces a person's blood pressure. 是科研结论句，常用 significantly 表达「显著降低血压」——这是研究类英语的高频搭配。
H)intrinsically义为「本质上」，与外在效果不搭 intrinsically 强调「内在属性」，但 reduces a person's blood pressure 描述的是可观测的外部效果，逻辑指向不一致；研究语境惯用 significantly 表统计学显著。
L) recover动词
help your heart ___ from stress
recover from stress=从压力中恢复 the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart __(33)__ from stress. 是医学/心理类英语固定表达，与本段「古典音乐降血压、护心」的主题完全契合。
E) hurt动词
it wouldn't ___ to do 句型，情态助动词后接动词原形

it wouldn't hurt to do = 做……不会有坏处 it wouldn't __(34)__ to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__. 是英语固定句式「it wouldn't hurt to do sth」，意为「不妨做某事/做……没坏处」，与作者鼓励读者抽空听音乐的语气完全匹配。

A)alleviate及物动词，需要直接宾语，与 to do 不配 alleviate 后必须接被缓解的对象（如 alleviate stress），而本句结构是 it wouldn't ___ to take…，空后没有宾语而是不定式短语，与 alleviate 的及物用法不匹配；且 26 题已用 A。 L)recover义为「恢复」，与「做某事不会有坏处」语义错位 it wouldn't recover to do 不构成英语习惯表达，recover 通常接 from / sth，且与作者「建议你抽空听听音乐」的语气也对不上；且 33 题已用 L。
N) soothing形容词
find + 宾语 + 空（宾语补足语）

music + soothing=令人舒缓的音乐 to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__. 与全文 The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect 形成首尾呼应，soothing 与 calming 同义，「舒缓的」音乐正是作者建议大家去听的类型。
F)inhibiting义为「抑制的」，感情色彩与劝勉语气冲突 inhibiting 带消极色彩，意为「让人放不开/受抑制」，与作者鼓励读者享受音乐、放松身心的结尾语气完全相反；命题人故意把它放进来当陷阱。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— find sth + 空，形容词诱惑+词性同位。inhibiting 和 soothing 同为 -ing 形容词，词性都对、都能修饰 music，区别仅在感情色彩；如果不回头核对全文「舒缓/愉悦」的基调，很容易掉坑。

longreading.title: 2024年6月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark—a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world. So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?
passages.zh: 在佐治亚州雅典市，有一处颇为奇特的当地地标——一棵几乎人人都说拥有自己的大白橡树。因此，它被认为是世界上最著名的树木之一。那么，这棵树究竟是如何拥有自己以及周围土地的呢？

passages.en: B) Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. It states, "Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human. Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it."
passages.zh: 据报道，19世纪的某个时候，一位名叫威廉·杰克逊上校的佐治亚州人喜欢上了这棵树，并努力保护它免受任何危险。至于他为何如此喜爱它，目前有文字记载的最早叙述，是《雅典周报》于1890年8月12日刊登的一篇匿名头版文章。文章写道：“杰克逊上校从童年起就看着这棵树长大，并逐渐像爱一个人那样爱上了它。它繁茂的枝叶和粗壮的树枝常常为他遮挡大雨，而在那最高的枝桠上，他曾多次找到鸣禽的鸟蛋。他注视着它的成长；当自己步入老年，看到这棵树以雄伟的姿态挺立时，一想到自己死后它可能会落入那些会毁掉它的人手中，他便感到痛苦。”

passages.en: C) Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. The deed read, "W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides."
passages.zh: 为了实现这一目的，杰克逊通过一份契据，将这棵树及其周围的一小块土地的所有权转让给了这棵树本身。契据上写道：“W. H. 杰克逊出于对上述树木的深厚感情，以及希望看到它受到保护的强烈愿望，特将该橡树本身及其四周八英尺以内的全部土地的完全占有权转让给该橡树。”

passages.en: D) In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians(看管者) of Earth. Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.
passages.zh: 随着时间推移，这棵树逐渐成了一个旅游景点，被称为“拥有自己的树”。然而，20世纪初，这棵树开始显现出缓慢死亡的迹象，人们对此几乎无能为力。最终，岁月会降临到我们每个人身上，即使是那些往往长寿、高大且枝叶繁茂的地球守护者也不例外。1942年10月9日，这棵高逾30米、树龄在200至400年之间的树倒下了；据传，它是由于一场强烈的风暴，和（或）此前已经死亡、根部腐烂所致。

passages.en: E) About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree. And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.
passages.zh: 大约四年后，初级女士园艺俱乐部的成员（她们曾在这棵树不幸死亡前照料过它）找到了一棵由原树果实中的一颗坚果培育而成的小树。于是，1946年10月9日，在佐治亚大学农业学院罗伊·鲍登教授的指导下，这棵小树被移植到了其祖先所在的位置。几个月后，人们举行了一场正式仪式，雅典市市长罗伯特·L·麦克沃特亲自出席，以纪念这一时刻。

passages.en: F) This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.
passages.zh: 这棵新树被称为“拥有自己的树之子”，人们认为，作为原树的继承者，它自然继承了自己所立之处的土地。当然，据知还有几十棵其他树木是原树的后代，因为人们拿走它的坚果并在别处培育成树是必然会发生的事。话虽如此，迄今为止，原树的其他子代没有一棵向法院请求分得土地，因此看来一切都没有问题。无论如何，“拥有自己的树之子”至今仍然屹立在那里，尽管人们常常只是把它称为“拥有自己的树”。

passages.en: G) This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.
passages.zh: 这一切最终都让我们不得不思考：杰克逊当初是否真的把这棵树的法定所有权转让给了它自己，以及这样的契据是否具有法律约束力。

passages.en: H) Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.
passages.zh: 首先，事实证明，杰克逊一生只在雅典市生活了大约三年，从1829年到1832年，开始居住时已经43岁。这在某种程度上否定了他从童年起就在树下度过时光、看着它成长，并担心自己死后它会遭遇什么的说法。此外，对雅典市土地所有权记录进行的广泛查找似乎表明，杰克逊从未拥有这棵树所在的土地。

passages.en: I) He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear. Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31, 000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.
passages.zh: 在那三年里，他确实住在紧挨着这棵树的一大片土地上，但尚不清楚那片土地是否归他所有。无论情况如何，1832年，一块四英亩的土地被出售给大学教授马尔萨斯·A·沃德；这块土地包括树木所在之地、杰克逊居住的相邻土地，以及其他土地。在这笔交易中，沃德被要求向杰克逊支付1200美元（按今天的价值约合3.1万美元），这笔钱要么是购买该地产的价款，要么只是对杰克逊在这块土地上所作改良的补偿。归根结底，无论杰克逊是否曾拥有相邻地块，还是只是在据称于大学任职期间获准使用该地块，他肯定从未拥有那棵树生长所在的地块，而这正是眼下这个话题中最重要的一点。

passages.en: J) After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.
passages.zh: 沃德教授买下土地后，杰克逊和他的家人在几英里外购买了一块655英亩的土地，并搬到了那里。十年后，也就是1844年，杰克逊似乎陷入了经济困境，他的小型种植园被克拉克县治安官办公室查封，并被拍卖以偿还抵押贷款。因此，假如他曾在雅典市拥有一些土地，包括那棵树所在的土地，那么他大概会把它卖掉以筹集资金，或者那块土地也会一并被查封。

passages.en: K) And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.
passages.zh: 无论实际情况如何，杰克逊都应该知道，要让契据所涉及的土地真正得到长期保障，就必须缴纳该土地的财产税。然而，没有任何账目或记录表明，曾设立过信托或类似安排来处理这件事。

passages.en: L) On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.
passages.zh: 除此之外，没有确凿证据表明这样的契据曾经存在过，尽管雅典市的契据记录可以追溯到杰克逊1876年去世前几十年，而且据那位声称见过该契据的匿名新闻记者所说，1890年时它本应还存放在档案中。

passages.en: M) As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?
passages.zh: 从上述一切情况来看，你或许可以想象，很少有人相信这一版本的故事。那么，这一切究竟是如何产生的呢？

passages.en: N) It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled "Deeded to Itself", which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.
passages.zh: 人们推测，这个故事是《雅典周报》那位匿名作者凭空想象出来的；该报此前于1890年刊登了一篇头版文章，标题为《转让给它自己》。顺便一提，那篇文章中有几个要素更容易被证明是虚假的。至于作者为何要这样做，人们推测，这或许是19世纪版本的“诱导点击式”思维练习，讨论的是把这样一种没有意识的生物转让给它自己是否合法。

passages.en: O) Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.
passages.zh: 无论如何，关于“拥有自己的树”的下一次已知记载，直到1901年才出现，刊载于同一份报纸《雅典周报》的百年纪念版中。该记载显然只是照抄了大约十年前刊登的原文，只稍作改写。下一次记载出现在1906年，同样刊载于《雅典周报》，也同样明显是对最初记载稍作改写后的翻抄，相当于19世纪版本的转发，因为读者已经忘记了原文。

statements.en: Jackson was said to have transferred his ownership of the oak tree to itself in order to protect it from being destroyed.
statements.zh: 据说Jackson将这棵橡树的所有权转让给了橡树本身,以保护它免遭破坏。

analysis.锚点: 为防止被毁而转让所有权
analysis.定位: C 段 Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. 为此，杰克逊通过一份契约的方式，把这棵树以及它周围一小片土地的所有权转让给了树本身。
analysis.改写: transferred his ownership of the oak tree to itself↔transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree ... to the tree itself 动作部分关键词原样复现 in order to protect it from being destroyed↔his great desire to see it protected 目的状语的同义替换 + 否定显隐
analysis.辨邻: B Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human 解释他为何爱树，是 C 段动作的情感铺垫，但本段并未出现『转让所有权』这一关键动作，因而不是源头段。 he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it

statements.en: No proof has been found from an extensive search that Jackson had ever owned the land where the oak tree grew.
statements.zh: 经过广泛搜索,没有找到证据证明Jackson曾经拥有过橡树生长所在的那片土地。

analysis.锚点: 大量检索无证据证明杰克逊拥有该地
analysis.定位: H 段 Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on. 此外，对雅典市土地所有权档案的一次大规模检索似乎也没能表明杰克逊曾经拥有过那棵树所在的土地。
analysis.改写: No proof has been found from an extensive search↔an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate 『未能表明』≈『没找到证据』的隐性否定 Jackson had ever owned the land where the oak tree grew↔Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on 几乎逐词对应
analysis.辨邻: L there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed 否定的是『契约存在过』，与题干 Jackson had ever owned the land 否定的是『他曾拥有土地』，否定的宾语完全不同，因而不是源头段。 there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed I he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on 虽然结论同向，但该段重点在四英亩交易与 1200 美元，并未点出『大规模档案检索』这一题干硬锚点；因而只是局部相关，不是 37 题的源头段。 he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand

statements.en: When it was raining heavily, Jackson often took shelter under a big tree that is said to own itself.
statements.zh: 下大雨时,Jackson经常在一棵据说拥有自己的大树下避雨。

analysis.锚点: 下大雨时常在树下避雨
analysis.定位: B 段 Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. 这棵树茂密的枝叶和粗壮的枝条常常把他从大雨中庇护下来，他还多次从最高的枝头上掏过鸣禽的蛋。
analysis.改写: When it was raining heavily↔from the heavy rains 时间从句压缩成名词短语 Jackson often took shelter under a big tree↔Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him 主动『他避雨』≈ 被动『树庇护他』
analysis.辨邻: C Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree 与下雨场景毫不相干，C 段只共享专名 Jackson 与同一棵树，不承载题干的雨中避雨细节。 his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself

statements.en: There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes for the land on which the oak tree sat.
statements.zh: 没有证据表明Jackson曾安排为橡树所在的土地缴纳财产税。

analysis.锚点: 无证据证明他为缴财产税做过安排
analysis.定位: K 段 Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this. 然而没有任何说法或记录显示曾设立过任何信托之类的安排来落实这一点。
analysis.改写: There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes↔no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this 抽象的『安排』下位化为具体的『信托』 for the land on which the oak tree sat↔property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land 『树所在地』≈『契约所及之地』
analysis.辨邻: L there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed 否定的是契约本身的存在，与题干 to pay property taxes 这一税务安排无关，不是源头段。 there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed

statements.en: Professor Ward paid Jackson over one thousand dollars when purchasing a piece of land from him.
statements.zh: Ward教授从Jackson手中购买一块土地时向他支付了一千多美元。

analysis.锚点: Ward 教授付杰克逊一千多美元
analysis.定位: I 段 In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31,000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. 在这笔交易中，Ward 被要求付给杰克逊 1200 美元（按今天的币值约 3.1 万美元），要么作为这处地产本身的款项，要么仅作为对杰克逊在该地块上所做改良的补偿。
analysis.改写: Professor Ward paid Jackson over one thousand dollars↔Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 $1,200 落在『一千多美元』的范围里 when purchasing a piece of land from him↔a four acre parcel ... was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward 『从他这里买地』对应『四英亩地块卖给 Ward』
analysis.辨邻: J had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage 讲的是杰克逊家庄园被法警拍卖偿债，没有出现 Ward 也没有具体金额，与题干 Professor Ward paid Jackson 的人物方向相反，属于话题相邻但人物方向不符。 had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage

statements.en: It is said the tree that owned itself fell in a heavy windstorm.
statements.zh: 据说这棵拥有自己的树在一场强风暴中倒下了。

analysis.定位: D 段 Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted. 最终在 1942 年 10 月 9 日，这棵超过 30 米高、树龄 200 至 400 年的大树倒下了；传言说是由于一场强风暴，又或是因为它早已死去、树根烂掉所致。
analysis.改写: the tree that owned itself fell↔the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell 关键动词 fell 原样复现 in a heavy windstorm↔as a result of a severe windstorm heavy ≈ severe 的同义替换

statements.en: The story of the oak tree is suspected to have been invented as a thought exercise.
statements.zh: 关于这棵橡树的故事被怀疑是作为一个思想实验而编造出来的。

analysis.定位: N 段 As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not. 至于作者为什么这么干，有人猜测，这或许是 19 世纪版的标题党式思想实验：探讨把这种没有意识的活物所有权授予它自己在法律上是否可行。
analysis.改写: The story of the oak tree is suspected to have been invented↔It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author suspected ≈ speculated 的同义替换 as a thought exercise↔a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise thought exercise 关键术语原样复现
analysis.辨邻: M So how did all of this come about then? 只是过渡反问，没有提到 thought exercise，未承载题干的核心断言，因而不是源头段。 few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?

statements.en: Jackson's little plantation was auctioned off to settle his debt in the mid-19th century.
statements.zh: Jackson的小种植园在19世纪中叶被拍卖以偿还他的债务。

analysis.锚点: 19 世纪中叶小庄园被拍卖抵债
analysis.定位: J 段 Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. 十年后即 1844 年，杰克逊似乎陷入了财务困境，他那座小庄园被克拉克县治安官办公室没收并拍卖以偿还按揭。
analysis.改写: Jackson's little plantation was auctioned off↔had his little plantation ... auctioned off 关键短语原样复现 to settle his debt↔to settle the mortgage debt 与 mortgage 的上下位 in the mid-19th century↔Ten years later, in 1844 1844 年落在 19 世纪中叶
analysis.辨邻: I a four acre parcel ... was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward 是 1832 年的正常出售，既不是『auctioned off』，年份也偏早（19 世纪上半叶早期，并非中叶），与题干 auctioned off to settle his debt in the mid-19th century 不符。 in 1832 a four acre parcel ... was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward

statements.en: An official ceremony was held to celebrate the transplanting of a small tree to where its ancestor had stood.
statements.zh: 举行了一场官方仪式来庆祝一棵小树移植到其祖先曾经站立的地方。

analysis.锚点: 为小树移植到原址举行了官方仪式
analysis.定位: E 段 A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion. 几个月后还举行了一场正式仪式，由雅典市市长 Robert L McWhorter 亲自出席，以纪念这一时刻。
analysis.改写: An official ceremony was held↔an official ceremony was held 关键短语原样复现 to celebrate the transplanting of a small tree↔this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor celebrate 由 commemorate 同义替换；the occasion 指向移植 where its ancestor had stood↔to the location of its ancestor 地点状语的句式重构
analysis.辨邻: F This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on 讲的是新树继承土地的故事，与题干 An official ceremony 的官方仪式不在同一事件，属于话题相邻而非源头段。 This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself

statements.en: The story of the Tree That Owns Itself appeared in the local paper several times, with slight alterations in wording.
statements.zh: 关于拥有自己的树的故事在当地报纸上出现过几次,措辞略有改动。

analysis.锚点: 故事在当地报纸多次出现、措辞略改
analysis.定位: O 段 This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original. 这（1901 年那一期）刊登了另一篇报道，明显只是抄录大约十年前的那篇原始报道，只是稍作改写。下一次出现在 1906 年，又是登在 Athens Weekly Banner 上，又是明显抄录原文，只是稍作改写；这相当于 19 世纪版的『读者忘了原帖后再发一遍』。
analysis.改写: appeared in the local paper several times↔the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 ... The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner 枚举多次出现 = several times with slight alterations in wording↔only slightly reworded 名词化短语对应到副词 + 过去分词
analysis.辨邻: N It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article 讨论的是文章被虚构的动机，与题干 appeared in the local paper several times 的『多次出现』不是同一事件，属于话题相邻但角度不同。 It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner

passages.en: It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?
passages.zh: 不可否认，员工知道是非对错。那么，为什么当他们看到有人在工作场所表现出可能导致事故的行为时，却没有更多员工出面干预呢？

passages.en: There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.
passages.zh: 有许多因素会影响人们是否进行干预。首先，他们需要能够看出危险情形正在逐渐发生。其次，公司的文化需要让他们感到可以安全地表达意见。第三，他们需要具备有效表达的沟通技巧。

passages.en: This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect—the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
passages.zh: 这并不完全是工作场所的问题；在工作之外，这也日益成为一个严重的问题。人们每天都会目睹街头发生的事情，却选择袖手旁观。这被称为旁观者效应——目睹某一事件的人越多，群体中的任何人出手帮助受害者的可能性就越小。这背后的心理机制被称为责任分散。基本而言，人群越大，越多人会认为其他人会处理这件事，这意味着在需要帮助的时刻，没有人真正进行干预或采取行动。

passages.en: This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.
passages.zh: 这种群体心态强烈到足以让人们逃避自己明知应承担的责任。但在工作场所不进行安全干预的并不只有一线员工，也有主管不进行干预的情况。

passages.en: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
passages.zh: 当一群员工看到领导层没有处理不安全行为时，就会形成一种先例，使人们认为这类情况就应该这样处理，从而为所有人确立安全文化。

passages.en: Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.
passages.zh: 尽管人们被鼓励在发现不安全作业时进行干预，但实际发生这种干预的情况还不到一半。不进行干预的最终原因是恐惧：害怕受到惩罚，害怕一旦进行干预就不得不承担更多工作。过去不成功的尝试也是人们不进行干预的重要原因之一——对于今后遇到的所有类似情况，他们往往更愿意把采取行动的责任推给别人。

passages.en: On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger.
passages.zh: 在许多工作场所，必须指定合格人员。他们的工作之一，就是在工人未配备适当设备进行作业或作业条件不安全时进行干预。当存在危险时，合格人员还必须叫停作业，不得继续进行。

passages.en: Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
passages.zh: 主管同样发挥着关键作用。即使不要求指定合格人员，主管也需要具备广泛的技能，不仅要能够识别和消除工作场所的危险，还要在团队内部营造一种安全氛围，支持成员之间进行干预和开放沟通。

passages.en: Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.
passages.zh: 除了合格人员和主管之外，重要的是要教育组织内的每一个人：无论你是指定的合格人员、主管还是一线员工，只要目睹了可能存在的不安全行为，就有义务进行干预。

questions.stem: What is one of the factors contributing to failure of intervention in face of risky behavior in the workplace?
questions.stem_zh: 在面对工作场所风险行为时,导致干预失败的因素之一是什么?

questions.判型: What is one of the factors contributing to failure of intervention in face of risky behavior in the workplace? 用 What 直接问一个具体因素，答案落点为原文明确给出的某项 factor，是典型客观细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干为 What is one of the factors，后接现在分词短语 contributing to failure of intervention 作定语修饰 factors，再用介词短语 in face of risky behavior in the workplace 限定场景。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. 第二，公司的文化需要让他们觉得发声是安全的。

locate.en: Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up.
locate.zh: 第二，公司的文化需要让他们觉得发声是安全的。

原文说「需要文化让人敢说」，预判答案是「文化不让人敢说」，B 项 Unfavorable workplace culture 正是这一缺失态的同义改写，因此锁定 B。

pairs.orig: the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up

option_analysis.note: they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold 说的是「员工要能预见风险」，而 Unforeseeable risk 反过来说「风险无法预见」，与原文方向相反；且不在 P2 的三因素列表中。
they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively 说的是「需要具备沟通技能」，强调的是个人技能层面；而 Blocked communication 说「沟通被阻塞」，把「技能不足」偷换为「通道被堵」，对象完全不同。

questions.stem: What does the author mean by "diffusion of responsibility" (Para. 3)?
questions.stem_zh: 作者所说的"责任分散"(第3段)是什么意思?

options.text: The more people are around, the more they need to worry about their personal safety.
options.zh: 周围的人越多,他们就越需要担心自己的人身安全。

options.text: The more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone will venture to
options.zh: 目睹某一事件的人越多,任何人冒险的可能性就越小。

options.text: The more people idling around on the street, the more likely they need taking care of.
options.zh: 在街上闲逛的人越多,他们就越有可能需要被照顾。

options.text: The more people are around, the less chance someone will step forward to intervene.
options.zh: 周围的人越多,有人站出来干预的机会就越少。

questions.判型: What does the author mean by 是经典的释义提问框架，答案为原文对该术语的同义解释。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does the author mean by，by 后跟引号词作宾语，括号内 (Para. 3) 为定位提示。结构清晰，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need. 基本上，人群越大，越多人就假定别人会处理这事——也就是说，在需要出手时反而无人有效干预或行动。

locate.en: Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
locate.zh: 基本上，人群越大，越多人就假定别人会处理这事——也就是说，在需要出手时反而无人有效干预或行动。

option_analysis.note: they need to worry about their personal safety 把原文「无人干预他人」的话题偷换成「担心自身安全」，自身安全在 P3 里根本未提及。

The more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone will venture to 后半句 venture to 后无宾语，句子残缺；即便补全也只是 the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim 的 bystander effect 释义，而题干问的是 diffusion of responsibility 这一更深层心理机制，对应的是 P3 后半句而非这句。
people idling around on the street 把原文 stand idly by 的「袖手旁观者」读成「街上闲逛的人」，并称他们「需要被照顾」，与 diffusion of responsibility 的心理机制无关。
选项 D 的两段比较级与原文的两段比较级一一对应：人多→人多假定→更少人出手干预，与预判「越多越没人挺身而出」严丝合缝，故锁定 D。

pairs.orig: the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it
pairs.opt: The more people are around, the less chance someone will step forward to intervene

questions.stem: What happens when unsafe behavior at the workplace is not addressed by the leaders?
questions.stem_zh: 当工作场所的不安全行为没有被领导者处理时,会发生什么?

options.text: No one will intervene when they see similar behaviors.
options.zh: 当人们看到类似行为时,没有人会进行干预。

options.text: Everyone will see it as the easiest way to deal with crisis.
options.zh: 每个人都会把它视为处理危机最简单的方法。

options.text: Workers have to take extra caution executing their duties.
options.zh: 工人在执行职责时必须格外谨慎。

options.text: Workers are left to take care of the emergency themselves.
options.zh: 工人只能自己处理紧急情况。

questions.判型: What happens when unsafe behavior at the workplace is not addressed by the leaders? 问「当条件 X 成立时结果是什么」，答案为原文明文给出的客观后果。
questions.拆句: 主干 What happens when，when 引导时间/条件状语从句，从句主语 unsafe behavior at the workplace，谓语为被动语态 is not addressed by the leaders。注意被动否定结构，主体是「领导层不去处理」。
questions.定位: P5 When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone. 当一群员工看到领导层不处理不安全行为时，就会形成「这类情况就该这样处理」的先例，从而为所有人定义了安全文化。

locate.en: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
locate.zh: 当一群员工看到领导层不处理不安全行为时，就会形成「这类情况就该这样处理」的先例，从而为所有人定义了安全文化。

option_analysis.note: 结合上下文（领导没干预+形成先例），先例的具体内容就是「对类似行为不干预」，选项 A 正是该先例的客观转述，故锁定 A。

pairs.orig: it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed
pairs.opt: No one will intervene when they see similar behaviors

option_analysis.note: 原文只说形成「该这样处理」的先例，并未评价它是 the easiest way；且「危机处理」角度也是 crisis 强加的描述。
Workers have to take extra caution 在原文中找不到根据，原文是说大家集体不干预，并非「工人变得更小心」。
Workers are left to take care of the emergency themselves 说工人会自己去处理紧急情况，而 P5 的逻辑是「没人去处理」，方向完全相反。

questions.stem: What is the ultimate reason workers won't act when they see unsafe operations?
questions.stem_zh: 当工人看到不安全操作时不采取行动的根本原因是什么?

options.text: Preference of deferring the action to others.
options.zh: 倾向于把行动推给其他人。

options.text: Anticipation of leadership intervention.
options.zh: 期待领导层进行干预。

options.text: Fear of being isolated by coworkers.
options.zh: 担心被同事孤立。

options.text: Fear of having to do more work.
options.zh: 害怕必须做更多工作。

questions.判型: What is the ultimate reason workers won't act when they see unsafe operations? 直问最终原因，答案为原文一句明文判断，非推断。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is the ultimate reason，后接省略了 why/that 的定语从句 workers won't act，再嵌套时间状语从句 when they see unsafe operations。注意「won't act」等价于「don't intervene」。
questions.定位: P6 Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. 恐惧是不干预的最终因素。存在对惩罚的恐惧，以及对「一旦干预就得做更多工作」的恐惧。

locate.en: Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene.
locate.zh: 恐惧是不干预的最终因素。存在对惩罚的恐惧，以及对「一旦干预就得做更多工作」的恐惧。

option_analysis.note: Preference of deferring the action to others 对应 they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations，但这是 Unsuccessful attempts in the past（过去失败经验）的副产品，是 another strong contributing factor，不是 ultimate factor。
Anticipation of leadership intervention 在 P6 没有依据。文中 P4 P5 提到 leadership 不干预，但谈的是「领导自己不出手」形成先例，而非「员工等领导干预」。
Fear of being isolated by coworkers 中「被同事孤立」在 P6 罗列的几种 fear（penalty / do more work / unsuccessful attempts）中并无对应。
原文罗列了两类 fear，选项 D 把第二类「怕多干活」原样收纳，与预判完全一致，故锁定 D。

pairs.orig: a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene
pairs.opt: Fear of having to do more work

questions.stem: What is critical to ensuring workplace safety?
questions.stem_zh: 什么对于确保工作场所安全至关重要?

options.text: Workers be trained to operate their equipment properly.
options.zh: 工人接受培训以正确操作设备。

options.text: Workers exhibiting at-risk behavior be strictly disciplined.
options.zh: 表现出危险行为的工人受到严格惩戒。

options.text: Supervisors create a safety environment for timely intervention.
options.zh: 监督者创造一个安全环境以便及时干预。

options.text: Supervisors conduct effective communication with frontline workers.
options.zh: 监督者与一线工人进行有效沟通。

questions.判型: What is critical to ensuring workplace safety? 问「对确保职场安全至关重要的是什么」，答案为原文显式给出的某项做法，非主旨概括。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is critical to ensuring workplace safety?，critical to 后接动名词短语 ensuring workplace safety 作介词宾语。注意 to 是介词不是不定式，故跟动名词。结构无陷阱。
questions.定位: P8 Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them. 主管也起着至关重要的作用。即便不需要专门的胜任人员，主管也需要一整套技能，既要能识别和消除职场隐患，也要在团队中营造支持干预和坦诚沟通的安全氛围。

locate.en: Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
locate.zh: 主管也起着至关重要的作用。即便不需要专门的胜任人员，主管也需要一整套技能，既要能识别和消除职场隐患，也要在团队中营造支持干预和坦诚沟通的安全氛围。

option_analysis.note: Workers be trained to operate their equipment properly 中「培训工人正确操作设备」在原文中无对应；without the proper equipment 谈的是「没有合适设备」，与「培训操作设备」不是一回事。
Workers exhibiting at-risk behavior be strictly disciplined 中「对有风险行为的工人进行严厉惩戒」，P6 只是说工人怕 penalty，不代表全文主张要 strictly discipline，原文并未把「严厉惩戒」作为确保安全的做法。
主语对位（Supervisors↔Supervisors）、动作对位（build↔create）、对象对位（safety climate↔safety environment）、目的对位（supports intervening↔for timely intervention），与预判一致，故锁定 C。

pairs.orig: build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening
pairs.opt: Supervisors create a safety environment for timely intervention

option_analysis.note: Supervisors conduct effective communication with frontline workers 抓住了 open communication，但漏掉原文核心 build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening——主管的关键不仅是沟通，而是建立支持干预的安全氛围；且 communication with frontline workers 把原文 open communication among them（团队内部沟通）偷换为「主管与一线工人之间的沟通」，对象错位。

reading2.title: 2024年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
passages.zh: “环保主义者”一词可以指不同的人。过去，它指的是试图保护野生动物和自然生态系统的人。在21世纪，这一词语的含义发生了变化，涵盖了应对人为造成的气候变化的需要。

passages.en: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
passages.zh: 这两种环保主义之间的区别，是科学界围绕核能问题产生分歧的原因。

passages.en: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
passages.zh: 一方是信奉纯粹主义的人，他们认为核电的风险不值得承担，应对气候危机的唯一方案就是可再生能源。另一方则同意可再生能源至关重要，但表示，当阳光不照耀、风也不吹动时，社会仍需要有足够的电力来满足消费者的基本需求。核能比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多，因此是一种自然的选择，尤其是在水力发电能力有限的地方。

passages.en: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
passages.zh: 曾参与撰写联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会报告的莱昂·克拉克，并不是毫无保留地支持核能，但他说，如果我们认真对待实现碳中和这一目标，那么核能是一个值得保留的选择。

passages.en: "Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."
passages.zh: 他说：“这一切的核心在于，你认为我们究竟有多大可能仅凭100%的可再生能源实现气候目标。如果你不相信我们能够做到，同时又关心气候问题，那么你就不得不考虑核能之类的方案。”

passages.en: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
passages.zh: 实现普遍的100%可再生能源同样存在争议。佛蒙特州的伯灵顿等城市，多年来一直实现了“100%可再生能源”。但这些城市往往人口较少，有时仍然依赖化石燃料能源，而且手头拥有丰富的可再生能源资源。与此同时，那些成功依靠可再生能源运行的国家，通常也是得益于非同寻常的水力发电能力。

passages.en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.
passages.zh: 德国是大型工业化国家推进绿色能源的最佳案例研究对象。德国总理安格拉·默克尔于2011年宣布实施“能源转型”，逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时逐步引入可再生能源。自2010年以来，风能和太阳能发电量增加了400%以上，2019年可再生能源占该国发电量的46%。

passages.en: But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
passages.zh: 但近年来，进展已经停滞。可再生能源的不稳定性不仅意味着夜间经常无法发电，还意味着太阳能和风能在白天可能使电网超负荷，迫使公用事业公司付钱给用户，让他们使用这些电力。滞后的电网基础设施难以将过剩的绿色能源从德国北部输送到工业发达的南部，这意味着许多工厂仍然依靠煤炭和天然气运行。在一些地方，政治上的容忍度也已达到极限，居民以激烈的抗议回应新风力涡轮机的建设。

passages.en: The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
passages.zh: 结果是，自2010年以来，德国的温室气体排放量下降了约11.5%，低于欧盟13.5%的平均降幅。

questions.stem: What accounts for the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy?
questions.stem_zh: 是什么造成了科学界内部关于核能的分歧?

options.text: Attention to combating human-made climate change.
options.zh: 对应对人为气候变化的关注。

options.text: Emphasis on protecting wildlife and natural ecosystems.
options.zh: 对保护野生动物和自然生态系统的重视。

options.text: Evolution of the term "green energy" over the last century.
options.zh: 过去一个世纪"绿色能源"一词的演变。

options.text: Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism.
options.zh: 对环境保护主义不同解释的坚持。

questions.判型: What accounts for the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy? 问的是"分裂的原因是什么"，是对原文具体因果关系的客观追问。
questions.拆句: Q51 主语是疑问词 What，谓语 accounts for（=解释/导致），宾语是 the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy，about 短语限定 divide 的具体领域。结构清晰、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy. 这两种环保主义之间的区别，正是科学界在核能问题上发生分裂的原因。

locate.en: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
locate.zh: 这两种环保主义之间的区别，正是科学界在核能问题上发生分裂的原因。

option_analysis.note: Attention to combating human-made climate change 只对应 P1 里 environmentalist 的"第二种含义"，不是"两种含义的差异"。
Emphasis on protecting wildlife and natural ecosystems 只对应 P1 里 environmentalist 的"第一种含义"，同样只覆盖单侧。
原文谈的是 The term "environmentalist" 在 21 世纪的演变，Evolution of the term "green energy" over the last century 把术语换成了 green energy、时间换成了 the last century。
预判要求答案体现"对环保主义的不同理解→科学界分裂"这一因果链，Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism 是四项中唯一精准覆盖该因果的表述。

pairs.orig: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism
pairs.opt: Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism

questions.stem: What is the solution to energy shortage proposed by purists' opponents?
questions.stem_zh: 纯粹主义者的反对者提出的能源短缺解决方案是什么?

options.text: Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively.
options.zh: 坚定且专门依赖可再生能源。

options.text: Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately.
options.zh: 交替使用化石燃料和绿色能源。

options.text: Opting for nuclear energy when necessary.
options.zh: 必要时选择核能。

options.text: Limiting people's non-basic consumption.
options.zh: 限制人们的非基本消费。

questions.判型: What is the solution to energy shortage proposed by purists\' opponents? 问对立方提出的具体方案，是原文已有的客观表述。
questions.拆句: Q52 主干 What is the solution，to energy shortage 修饰 solution，过去分词短语 proposed by purists\' opponents 后置修饰 solution。注意 purists\' 是所有格，opponents 才是真正的主语方。
questions.定位: P3 The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited. 对立方认同可再生能源关键，但表示在阳光不足、无风时社会仍需一定量电力以满足消费者的基本需求。核能比油、气、煤都清洁得多，是自然之选，尤其在水电能力有限的地方。

locate.en: The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
locate.zh: 对立方认同可再生能源关键，但表示在阳光不足、无风时社会仍需一定量电力以满足消费者的基本需求。核能比油、气、煤都清洁得多，是自然之选，尤其在水电能力有限的地方。

option_analysis.note: Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively 描述的恰恰是 purists 的立场，而非对立方——对立方主张的是核能补缺，绝不"独占"可再生能源。
Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately 谈"化石燃料和绿色能源交替使用"，原文从未提出过"交替使用"这一方案，且对立方明确说核能 far cleaner than oil, gas and coal，即反对烧煤气油。
预判结论"必要时启用核能补缺"在四项中只有 Opting for nuclear energy when necessary 精准匹配。

pairs.orig: Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited
pairs.opt: Opting for nuclear energy when necessary

option_analysis.note: Limiting people\'s non-basic consumption 谈"限制非基本消费"，原文只提 consumers\' basic demands——"满足基本需求"和"限制非基本消费"是两回事，后者属凭空引申。

questions.stem: What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example?
questions.stem_zh: 作者想以Burlington等城市为例说明什么观点?

options.text: It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world's exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable.
options.zh: 全世界完全依赖可再生能源的目标是否可以实现是有争议的。

options.text: It is contentious whether cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal.
options.zh: 人口众多的城市是否拥有可直接利用的可再生资源是有争议的。

options.text: It is arguable whether cities that manage to run off renewables have sustainable hydroelectric capabilities.
options.zh: 设法依靠可再生能源运行的城市是否拥有可持续的水力发电能力是有争议的。

options.text: It is debatable whether traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world.
options.zh: 传统化石燃料能源是否能在全世界范围内被完全淘汰是有争议的。

questions.判型: What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example? 直接问"举这个例子是为了说明什么"，是典型例证目的题。
questions.拆句: Q53 主干 What point does the author want to make，介词短语 with cities like Burlington as an example 作伴随状语，说明作者作出该 point 时所凭借的例子。with…as… 是"以……作为……"的固定结构。
questions.定位: P6 The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. 全球 100% 可再生能源是否能实现同样有争议。像佛蒙特州 Burlington 这样的城市多年来一直号称"100% 可再生"。

locate.en: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years.
locate.zh: 全球 100% 可再生能源是否能实现同样有争议。像佛蒙特州 Burlington 这样的城市多年来一直号称"100% 可再生"。

option_analysis.note: 预判结论包含三要素"全球范围、独占可再生、可达成性存疑"，A 是四项中唯一同时覆盖三要素的表述。

pairs.orig: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious
pairs.opt: It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world\'s exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable

option_analysis.note: cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal 谈"大人口城市是否有可再生资源"，原文 P6 只说 Burlington 这类"小人口"城市，并未把议题转向"大人口城市能否做到"。

原文 countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities 只说"靠可再生运转的国家"通常水电禀赋强，并未质疑其"可持续性"；选项 sustainable hydroelectric capabilities 把客观描述偷换为"是否可持续"的争议。
traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world 谈"是否能在全球范围彻底废除化石燃料"，原文只论"是否能 100% 可再生"，并未直接讨论"彻底废除化石燃料"，两者虽相关但不等价。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy?
questions.stem_zh: 关于可再生能源,我们对德国有何了解?

options.text: It has increased its wind and solar power generation four times over the last two decades.
options.zh: 在过去二十年里,它的风能和太阳能发电量增加了四倍。

options.text: It represents a good example of a major industrialized country promoting green energy.
options.zh: 它代表了一个主要工业化国家推广绿色能源的良好范例。

options.text: It relies on renewable energy to generate more than half of its electricity.
options.zh: 它依靠可再生能源产生超过一半的电力。

questions.判型: What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy? 是对原文中关于德国可再生能源相关事实的复核问题。
questions.拆句: Q54 主干 What do we learn about Germany，regarding renewable energy 介词短语限定话题范围（regarding=关于）。句式平铺，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P7 Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. 德国是大型工业化国家推进绿色能源的最佳案例。

locate.en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy.
locate.zh: 德国是大型工业化国家推进绿色能源的最佳案例。

option_analysis.note: 原文 Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010 是"自 2010 年以来"约 10 年，而 over the last two decades 是"过去二十年"——时间维度被夸大一倍。
预判结论"大型工业国推进绿能的范本"与 B 在主谓宾每个成分上都做到同义替换，是最高质量的同义匹配。

pairs.orig: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy
